draft.text: You came in because you have had a constant ache in your right knee since a fall two weeks ago.
The pain is on the inside of your knee, along the medial joint line, and it is tender to touch.
You feel some instability and shifting when walking, but no locking, catching, or giving way of the knee.
Ligament testing showed a little laxity in the posterior drawer test, but the anterior drawer test was negative.
You have a soft clicking sensation in your knee when bending or straightening it.
The clicking is not accompanied by difficulty in bending or straightening, but you may feel stiff, especially in the morning.
The doctor will review the MRI results and discuss the findings with you.
The best course of treatment based on the MRI results will be discussed with you.

unverified_summary.text: You came in because you have had a constant ache in your right knee since a fall two weeks ago.
Your knee is tender on the inside along the medial joint line.
You feel instability and shifting when walking.
X-rays showed no significant problems, but there was a little laxity in the posterior drawer test.
You may have an injury to the posterior cruciate ligament in your right knee.
This could be causing your pain and feeling of instability.
You will have an MRI to check for possible meniscus tear or cartilage damage.
The doctor will look at the results and talk to you about what they mean and next steps.
